answer_1.quote: We employed 24 LLMs ... using contests from the arena-human-preference-55k dataset, which contains a collection of unique prompts crowdsourced by real human users, paired responses to each prompt from two competing LLMs ... including less well-defined ones ... such as complex textual tasks like translation.
answer_1.outputs: pairwise preference judgments (wins/ties) derived from LLM judges

answer_2.quote: We propose that an LLM's Consistency ... can serve as a proxy for measuring its own Elo score, without requiring human feedback or prior knowledge of the task.

answer_3.quote: We employ a two-stage chain-of-thought prompting process to elicit preferences from LLMs judging a given contest.
methods: two-stage chain-of-thought prompting for pairwise evaluation

answer_4.quote: Although this dataset also includes human preference annotations, these were not used in our study.
